canonical_name: Hyperbolic parallel postulate (repository family label; exact proposition open)
literal_source_claim_zh: 过直线外一点可作无数条平行线
literal_source_claim_en: Through a point outside a line, infinitely many parallel lines can be drawn.
statement_blocker: The catalog does not identify an immutable source, ambient synthetic geometry or analytic model, incidence and betweenness axioms, line type and equality, external-point predicate, parallel convention, line distinctness, logical role as axiom or derived theorem, or meaning of infinitely many. Disjoint, limiting, asymptotic, and ultraparallel conventions differ, and existence of at least two parallels is not definitionally the literal infinite-family claim. Selecting a familiar formulation would add or substitute proposition-changing mathematics.
domain_and_universes: Open: an approved source must fix the point and line universes, ambient synthetic axiom structure or analytic model, incidence, betweenness and congruence relations, complete-geodesic representation, line equality or quotient, boundary and ideal-point treatment, and all required typeclass data.
conclusion: Open: the gloss suggests infinitude of distinct lines through an external point that are parallel to a given line, but does not fix the parallel predicate, the set being counted, or the exact infinitude/cardinality assertion.
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded at intake because no proposition is selected; the statement phase must resolve degenerate or empty lines, coincident line representations, points incident with the original line, limiting ideal endpoints, orientation, sides, duplicate parametrizations, and empty or low-dimensional models.

a theorem that the set of complete geodesics through an external point and disjoint from a given geodesic is infinite

the negation of Playfair uniqueness or of Euclid's fifth postulate
a continuum-cardinality classification of nonintersecting through-lines
degenerate_cases_to_resolve: point incident with versus external to the given line
empty, singleton, degenerate, or non-complete line representations
extensional equality of lines versus distinct parametrizations of the same image
finite intersection versus shared ideal endpoint at the model boundary

unoriented versus oriented lines and the two sides of the given line
at least two versus set-infinite versus countably or continuum many candidates
synthetic axiom assumed directly versus theorem derived in a selected model
